cues.en: Or I was one of the people who did it. That thing is called a captcha. And the reason it's there is to make sure that you, the entity filling out the form, are actually a human and not some sort of computer program that was written to submit the form millions and millions of times. The reason it works is because humans at least non visually impaired humans have no trouble reading these distorted, squiggly characters, whereas computer programs simply can't do it as well yet. So, for example, in the case of Ticketmaster, the reason you have to type these distorted characters is to prevent scalpers from writing a program that can buy millions of tickets two at a time. Capturas are used all over the Internet, and since they're used so often, a lot of times the precise sequence of random characters that are shown to the user is not so fortunate.
cues.zh: 或者我是发明它的人之一。那东西叫验证码。它存在的目的，是确保填写表单的主体真的是人，而不是某种用来反复提交表单千百万次的计算机程序。它之所以有效，是因为人类——至少是没有视觉障碍的人类——读这些扭曲、弯弯曲曲的字符毫无困难，而计算机程序目前还做不到那么好。比如在 Ticketmaster 的例子里，你必须输入这些扭曲字符，是为了防止黄牛写程序一次两张地买走数百万张票。验证码在整个互联网上到处都在用，而因为用得太多，很多时候展示给用户的随机字符序列就不太走运了。

cues.en: see, here's the thing. While you're typing a CAPTCHA during those ten seconds, your brain is doing something amazing. Your brain is doing something that computers cannot yet do. So can we get you to do useful work for those ten seconds? Another way of putting it is, there's some humongous problem that we cannot yet get computers to solve, but that somehow we can split into tiny ten second chunks, such that each time somebody solves a CAPTCHA, they solve a little bit of this problem. The answer to that is yes, and this is what we're doing now. So what you may not know is that nowadays, while you're typing a captcha, not only are you authenticating yourself as a human, but in addition, you're actually helping us to digitize books.
cues.zh: 看，事情是这样的。当你在那十秒钟里输入验证码时，你的大脑正在做一件了不起的事。你的大脑正在做计算机还做不到的事。那么，我们能不能让你在这十秒钟里做些有用的工作？换个说法：有个巨大的问题，我们还没法让计算机解决，但不知怎么地能把它拆成一个个十秒钟的小块，这样每次有人解一个验证码，就解决了这个问题的一小部分。答案是肯定的，这就是我们现在在做的事。所以你可能不知道，如今你在输入验证码时，不仅是在验证自己是人类，而且实际上还在帮我们把书数字化。

cues.en: So let me explain how this works. There's a lot of projects out there trying to digitize books. Google has one. The Internet Archive has one. Amazon now with the Kindle is trying to digitize books. Basically, the way this works is you start with an old book, like a physical
cues.zh: 让我解释一下这是怎么运作的。外面有很多项目在尝试把书数字化。Google有一个。Internet Archive有一个。Amazon现在通过Kindle也在尝试把书数字化。基本上，做法是从一本旧书开始，就像一本实体

cues.en: Okay.

cues.en: So you start with a book, and then you scan it. Now, scanning a book is like taking a digital photograph of every page of the book. It gives you an image for every page of the book. This is an image with text for every page of the book. The next step in the process is that the computer needs to be able to decipher all of the words in this image. Done using a technology called OCR, for optical character recognition, which takes a picture of text and tries to figure out what the text is in there. Now, the problem is that OCR is not perfect. Especially for older books, where the ink has faded and the pages have turned yellow,
cues.zh: 所以你从一本书开始，然后扫描它。扫描一本书，就像给书的每一页拍一张数字照片。它会给你书每一页的图像。这是书每一页带有文字的图像。下一步，计算机需要能辨认出这张图像里的所有单词。这要用一种叫OCR的技术，也就是光学字符识别，它拍下文字图像并试着弄清里面是什么文字。现在的问题是，OCR并不完美。尤其是对旧书，墨迹已经褪色、书页已经发黄，

cues.en: OCR cannot recognize a lot of the words. For example, for things that were written more than fifty years ago, the computer cannot recognize about 30% of the words.
cues.zh: OCR无法识别很多单词。例如，对于五十多年前写的东西，计算机无法识别大约30%的单词。

cues.en: So what we're doing now is we're taking all of the words that the computer cannot recognize,
cues.zh: 所以我们现在做的是，把所有计算机无法识别的单词，

cues.en: and we're getting people to read them for us while they're typing a captcha on the Internet. So the next time you type a captcha, these words that you're typing are actually words that are coming from books that are being digitized that the computer cannot recognize.
cues.zh: 我们让人在互联网上输入验证码的时候顺便帮我们识别这些词。所以你下次输入验证码时，你打的这些词其实来自正在数字化的书籍中计算机无法识别的词。

cues.en: And now the reason we have two words nowadays instead of one is because, you see, one of the words is a word that the system just got out of a book. It didn't know what it was, and it's going to present it to you. But since it doesn't know the answer for it, it cannot grade it for you. So what we do is we give you another word, one for which the system does know the answer. We don't tell you which one's which, and we say, Please type both. And if you type the correct word for the one for which the system already knows the answer, it assumes you're human. And it also gets some confidence that you typed the other word correctly.
cues.zh: 现在之所以有两个单词而不是一个，是因为其中一个词是系统刚从书里扫出来的，它不知道这是什么词，要呈现给你。但既然它不知道答案，就没法给你评分。所以我们给你另一个词，这个词系统知道答案。我们不告诉你哪个是哪个，只说：请把两个都打出来。如果你把系统已知答案的那个词打对了，它就认定你是人类，同时也更有把握你另一个词也打对了。

cues.en: And if we repeat this process to 10 different people, and all of them agree on what the new word is, we get one more word digitized accurately.
cues.zh: 如果我们把这个过程重复给10个不同的人，他们都对新词给出同样的答案，我们就又准确数字化了一个词。

cues.en: So computer translation, not yet good enough. Okay, so back to the question. So we need people to translate the whole Web. Okay, so now the next question you may have is, well, why can't we just pay people to do this? We could pay professional language translators to translate the whole Web. We
cues.zh: 所以机器翻译还不够好。好，回到这个问题。我们需要有人翻译整个 Web。好，那么你接下来可能会问，为什么我们不能直接付钱让人来做这件事？我们可以雇专业翻译来翻译整个 Web。我们

cues.en: could do that. Unfortunately, would be extremely expensive.
cues.zh: 是可以这么做。但不幸的是，这会极其昂贵。

cues.en: For example, translating a tiny, tiny fraction of the whole Web Wikipedia
cues.zh: 例如，翻译整个 Web 中极小极小的一部分——Wikipedia

cues.en: into one other language Spanish.
cues.zh: 成另一种语言：西班牙语。

cues.en: You know, Wikipedia exists in Spanish, but it's very small compared to the size of English. It's about 20 the size of English. If we wanted to translate the other 80%
cues.zh: 你知道，Wikipedia 有西班牙语版本，但相比英语的规模它非常小。大约是英语规模的 20%。如果我们想翻译另外那 80%

cues.en: into Spanish, it would cost at least $50,000,000.
cues.zh: 成西班牙语，至少要花 5000 万美元。

cues.en: And this is even at the most exploited outsourcing country out there.
cues.zh: 而这还是在全球被压榨得最厉害的外包国家。

cues.en: So it would be very expensive. So what we want to do is get 100,000,000 people translated into every major language for free.
cues.zh: 所以成本会非常高。我们想做的是，免费把内容翻译成每种主要语言，让一亿人用上。

cues.en: Okay? Now, if this is what you want to do, you pretty quickly realize you're going to run into two pretty big hurdles, two big obstacles.
cues.zh: 对吧？如果你想做这件事，很快就会意识到会碰到两大障碍、两个大难题。

cues.en: Okay? The first one is a lack of bilinguals.
cues.zh: 第一个是缺少双语者。

cues.en: Okay? So
cues.zh: 对吧？所以

cues.en: I don't even know if there exist 100,000,000 people out there using the Web who are bilingual enough to help us translate.
cues.zh: 我甚至不知道网上是否存在一亿名双语能力足够强、能帮我们翻译的人。

cues.en: Okay, that's a big problem. The other problem that you're going to run into is a lack of motivation.
cues.zh: 好，这是个大问题。你还会碰到的另一个问题是缺少动力。

cues.en: How are we going to motivate people to actually translate the Web for free?
cues.zh: 我们怎么激励人们真的免费翻译网络内容？

cues.en: This is normally you have to pay people to do this, so how are we going to motivate them to do it for free? Now, when we were starting to think about this, we were blocked by these two things. But then we realized there's actually a way to solve both of these problems with the same solution. There's a way to kill two birds with one stone.
cues.zh: 通常这种事得付钱请人做，那我们怎么激励他们免费来做？一开始思考这件事时，我们被这两个问题卡住了。但后来我们意识到，其实有一种办法能同时解决这两个问题，能一石二鸟。

cues.en: And that is to transform language translation into something that millions of people want to do,
cues.zh: 那就是把语言翻译变成数百万人想做的事，

cues.en: and that also helps with the problem of lack of bilinguals,
cues.zh: 而且这还能帮助解决缺少双语者的问题，

cues.en: and that is language education.
cues.zh: 也就是语言教育。

cues.en: Okay? So it turns out that today there are over 1,200,000,000
cues.zh: 对吧？所以结果是，今天有超过12亿

cues.en: people learning a foreign language.
cues.zh: 人在学习外语。

cues.en: People really, really want to learn a foreign language, and it's not just because they're being forced to do so in school. For example, in The United States alone, there are over 5,000,000 people who have paid over $500 for software to learn a new language. So people really, really want to learn a new language. So what we've been working on for the last year and a half is a new website. It's called Duolingo,
cues.zh: 人们真的非常想学一门外语，而且不仅仅是因为在学校里被迫这么做。比如，仅在美国就有超过500万人付费超过500美元购买学习新语言的软件。所以人们真的非常想学一门新语言。因此，过去一年半我们一直在做的是一个新网站。它叫Duolingo，

cues.en: where the basic idea is people learn a new language for free while simultaneously translating the Web. And so basically, they're learning by doing.
cues.zh: 基本理念是让人们免费学习一门新语言，同时翻译网络内容。基本上，他们是在实践中学习。

cues.en: Okay, so the way this works is whenever you're just a beginner, we give you very, very simple sentences. There's, of course, a lot of very simple sentences on the Web. We give you very, very simple sentences along with what each word means.
cues.zh: 这个运作方式是，当你还是初学者时，我们会给你非常简单非常简单的句子。当然，网上有很多非常简单的句子。我们会给你非常简单的句子，并告诉你每个单词的意思。

cues.en: Okay? And as you translate them and as you see how other people translate them, you start learning the language. As you get more and more advanced, we give you more and more complex sentences to translate. But at all times you're learning by doing.
cues.zh: 好吗？当你翻译它们，并看到别人如何翻译时，你就开始学习这门语言了。随着你越来越进阶，我们会给你越来越复杂的句子来翻译。但始终你都是在实践中学习。

cues.en: Now the crazy thing about this method is that it actually really works.
cues.zh: 这个方法最疯狂的地方在于，它真的确实有效。

cues.en: First of all, people are really, really learning a language. We're mostly done building it and now testing it. People really can learn a language with it. And they learn it about as well as the leading language learning software. So people really do learn a language. And not only do they learn it as well, but actually it's way more interesting. Because you see, with Duolingo, people are actually learning with real content. As opposed to learning with made up sentences, people are learning with real content, which is inherently interesting.
cues.zh: 首先，人们真的在学一门语言。我们基本已经把它建好了，现在正在测试。人们真的可以用它学会一门语言。而且他们学得和领先的语言学习软件差不多好。所以人们真的学会了语言。不仅学得一样好，实际上还有趣得多。因为你看，用Duolingo，人们是在用真实内容学习。相比用编造的句子学习，人们是在用真实内容学习，而这本身就很有趣。

cues.en: The other thing so people really do learn a language. But perhaps more surprisingly,
cues.zh: 另一件事是，人们确实会学会一门语言。不过更令人惊讶的是，

cues.en: the translations that we get from people using the site, even though they're just beginners,
cues.zh: 即使只是初学者，他们在网站上提交的翻译，

cues.en: the translations that we get are as accurate as those of professional language translators, which is very surprising. So let me show you one example. This is a sentence that was translated from German into English. The top is the German. The middle is an English translation that was done by somebody who was a a professional language translator, who paid 20¢ a word for this translation. And the bottom is the translation by users of Duolingo,
cues.zh: 也能达到专业语言译者的准确度，这非常令人惊讶。让我展示一个例子。这是一句从德语翻译成英语的句子。最上面是德语；中间是专业语言译者完成的英语翻译，这份翻译的报酬是每词20美分；最下面是 Duolingo 用户的翻译，

cues.en: none of whom knew any German before they started using the site. You can see it's pretty much perfect. Now, of course, we play a trick here to make the translations as good as professional translators. We combine the translations of multiple beginners
cues.zh: 而且他们中没有任何人在使用网站之前懂德语。你可以看到，这几乎完美无误。当然，为了让翻译质量达到专业译者的水平，我们用了一个小技巧：把多个初学者的翻译结合起来

cues.en: to get the quality of a single professional translator.
cues.zh: 达到一名专业译者的质量。

cues.en: Now, even though we're combining
cues.zh: 虽然我们是在合并

cues.en: the translations,
cues.zh: 这些翻译，

cues.en: the site actually can translate pretty fast. Fast. So let me show you this is our estimates of how fast we could translate Wikipedia from English into Spanish.
cues.zh: 但这个网站实际上能非常快地完成翻译。非常快。让我展示一下，这是我们估算的把 Wikipedia 从英语翻译成西班牙语所需的速度。

cues.en: Remember, this is $50,000,000
cues.zh: 记住，这相当于价值5000万美元的内容。

cues.en: worth of value.
cues.zh: 这些内容的价值。

cues.en: So if we wanted to translate Wikipedia into Spanish, we could do it in five weeks with 100,000 active users, and we could do it in about eighty hours with a million active users. Since all the projects that my group has worked on so far have gotten millions of users, we're hopeful that we'll be able to translate extremely fast with this project.
cues.zh: 所以，如果我们想把 Wikipedia 翻译成西班牙语，10万名活跃用户只需五周，100万名活跃用户大约80小时就能完成。到目前为止，我们团队参与的所有项目都获得了数百万用户，因此我们希望这个项目也能实现极快的翻译速度。

cues.en: Now, the thing that I'm most excited about with Duolingo is that I think this provides a fair business model for language education.
cues.zh: 我对 Duolingo 最兴奋的一点是，我认为它为语言教育提供了一个公平的商业模式。

cues.en: So here's the thing. The current business model for language education is the student pays.
cues.zh: 事情是这样的。当前语言教育的商业模式是学生付费。

cues.en: And in particular, the student pays Rosetta Stone $500.
cues.zh: 具体来说，学生要付给 Rosetta Stone 500 美元。

cues.en: That's
cues.zh: 这就是

cues.en: the current business model. The problem with this business model is that 95%
cues.zh: 当前的商业模式。这个模式的问题在于，95%

cues.en: of the world's population doesn't have $500.
cues.zh: 的世界人口没有 500 美元。

cues.en: So it's extremely unfair
cues.zh: 所以这极不公平

cues.en: towards the poor. Okay? This is totally biased towards the rich. Now, see, in Duolingo,
cues.zh: 对穷人来说。对吧？这完全偏向富人。你看，在 Duolingo 里，

cues.en: because while you learn, you're actually creating value,
cues.zh: 因为你在学习的同时，其实也在创造价值，

cues.en: You are translating stuff, which, for example, we could charge somebody for translations. So this is how we could monetize this.
cues.zh: 你在翻译内容，比如我们可以向别人收取翻译费。这就是我们变现的方式。

cues.en: Since people are creating value while they're learning, they don't have to pay with their money. They pay with their time. But the magical thing here is that they're paying with their time, but that is time that would have to be spent anyways learning the language.
cues.zh: 既然人们在学习时创造价值，他们就不必用钱付费，而是用时间付费。但神奇的是，他们付出的是时间，而这段时间本来也一定要花在学习语言上。

cues.en: So the nice thing about Duolingo is I think it provides a fair business model, one that doesn't discriminate against poor people.
cues.zh: 所以 Duolingo 的好处在于，我认为它提供了一个公平的商业模式，不歧视穷人。

cues.en: So here's the site. Thank you.
cues.zh: 这就是网站。谢谢。

cues.en: So here's the site. We haven't yet launched,
cues.zh: 这就是网站。我们还没上线，

cues.en: but if you go there, you can sign up to be part of our private beta, which are probably going to start in about three or four weeks. We haven't yet launched Duolingo. By the way, I'm the one talking here. But actually, Duolingo is the work of a really awesome team, some of whom are here. So thank you.
cues.zh: 但如果你去那里，可以注册加入我们的内测，大概会在三四周后开始。我们还没上线 Duolingo。顺便说一句，现在讲话的人是我。但其实 Duolingo 是一个非常棒的团队做出来的，其中一些人就在这里。谢谢。
